Subject: MAP kickoff + evaluation milestones (proposal attached)

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. As discussed, I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan that ties the evaluation milestones to a small initial financial commitment and a clear renewal uplift path. High level: 

- Week 0–2: Access and engineering kickoff (no charge; sandbox).
- Week 3–6: Evaluation pilot (3 node, quantized) — $25k committed credit to cover burst/test traffic.
- Week 7–12: Ramp to 10M tokens/month; 6-month preferred pricing triggers 10% discount.
- Renewal year 1: Re-commit within 60 days of term end to keep pilot discount; uplift tiers defined in tab "Renewal Uplift".

Attachments: Pegasus_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP with milestones & linked pricing), redwood-eval-summary.pdf (ops profile & recommended config).

Action items I propose:
1) You confirm procurement/PO timeline so we can align billing start.
2) Tom — confirm whether a $25k committed credit is acceptable for the evaluation window.
3) Elena — confirm which SLAs you need documented in the SOW (we can add a specific failover clause for critical endpoints).

If that sounds right I can circulate a commercial one-pager and a simple signature page to speed procurement.

Best,
Ben Carter

Ben — thanks for the clear plan. A couple of procurement constraints from our side:

- Procurement needs a PO and vendor W-9; our security/compliance team will run an SOC2 quick review (target 7 business days).
- Finance is OK with an evaluation credit if we treat it as an upfront committed credit (not a refundable deposit).
- For renewals: we will only commit to a renewal uplift if we have demonstrable improvements on latency/cost per token vs our current infra during the pilot.

Question on pricing: the 10% discount at 10M tokens/month — can that be structured as a stepped discount (5% at 5M, 10% at 10M) so we have headroom during ramp? Also, is there a minimum term for Dedicated capacity?

I'll loop in Marcus (CFO) once we have a one-pager and PO template.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Procurement — Pegasus Health

Adding a couple of technical notes that affect the commercial structure: 

- The evaluation cluster we recommended (3 quantized nodes) will show ~30–40% cost reduction vs standard FP16 at inference volume >=2M tokens/month. That makes the stepped discount you asked for defensible — we can commit to a 5% effective discount at 5M, 10% at 10M when combined with caching & prefix reuse enabled.
- For renewal uplift: suggest we instrument a 30-day "re-eval" window 45 days before term end. If Pegasus opts to re-commit to a minimum 6-month reserved pool at that point, we apply the uplift schedule in the MAP (tiers listed in the Renewals tab).
- SLOs: I'll prepare an ops appendix with expected p95 p50 numbers and failover behaviour; this will speed the SOC2 review.

Elena / Tom — quick update and a proposed commercial path that incorporates your asks: 

Proposal (updated):
- Evaluation credit: $25k committed credit to be invoiced as a pre-paid credit (applied to first invoice).
- Stepped discount tiers: 5% at >=5M tokens/mo, 10% at >=10M tokens/mo (applied to metered hosted usage).
- Dedicated minimum term: 3-month reserved blocks with optional auto-renew; 6-month preferred for pricing guarantees.
- Renewal uplift: if Pegasus re-commits to a 6-month reserved pool within 60 days of contract end, previous discount tier preserved + additional 3% renewal uplift off list price for first renewal term.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Tom: share PO timing and vendor paperwork (we can provide W-9 and SOW appendix).
2) Elena: confirm acceptance of the $25k pre-paid credit model.
3) I'll circulate a commercial one-pager and an updated MAP with the renewal uplift rows highlighted.

Attaching: updated Pegasus_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP: commercial tabs updated).

If this aligns I can prepare the one-pager and a redlined SOW for your legal team.

Thanks,
